title: hardening: the daemon answers a /health challenge with an HMAC of a spawn key the IDE passed it, so VS Code can prove it started the daemon (prerequisite of task-648a5916)
description:
Prerequisite of task-648a5916, the CQ-RF07 residual about spawn provenance for VS Code under the protected profile. Split out by architect-24611a0a while planning that row, 2026-11-02.

Why: JetBrains proves it started a protected daemon from OS facts, (pid, startInstant) and the parent pid, via RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance. Node has no portable process start time, so VS Code needs a proof the daemon can give but cannot mint:
- VS Code mints a fresh 32-byte key for each protected spawn.
- It keeps the key in its owner-only store outside the repository (SecretStorage).
- It passes the key in the environment of the installed daemon it spawns.
- To verify, VS Code sends a fresh random challenge, and the daemon answers HMAC-SHA256(key, challenge).
A daemon started any other way holds no key and cannot answer. Examples: a terminal `node packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js start`, or a legacy seat's autostart. This is the spawn-nonce mechanism that docs/design/protected-profile-threat-model.md (CQ-RF05) lists as deferred. Same-user host processes stay outside that model, so the key's secrecy is not claimed against them.

Contract (packages/moe-daemon only; no MCP tool changes):
- Env `MOE_SPAWN_PROOF_KEY` holds exactly 64 hex characters (32 bytes).
  - The `_run` process reads it once at startup, keeps the bytes in memory, and deletes the variable from its own process.env, so nothing it spawns inherits it.
  - Any other value is ignored, with a log line that names the problem, never the value.
  - The `start` supervisor already passes process.env to every `_run` it spawns, crash restarts included (spawnChild, packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts ~:969). Keep that.
- `GET /health?challenge=<64 lowercase hex>` answers the normal body plus `spawnProof`, but only while a key is held. spawnProof is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the key bytes over the challenge's ASCII text.
  - No key, a missing, malformed or repeated challenge, or any other query parameter: the normal body without spawnProof.
  - The Host guard (isAllowedHealthHost) still runs first. Plain `GET /health` answers exactly as today, and every other path still answers 426.
- Known-answer vector, pinned identically by task-648a5916's client tests:
  - key 000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1f
  - challenge 'ab' repeated 32 times
  - spawnProof 583630234f7e60ecfa2a6ae2e98ee37876e3ff6344457723cb4b42fcf77f7fc0
- The key never reaches daemon.json, logs, the activity log, chat or any response.

Files: packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts, a new packages/moe-daemon/src/server/spawnProof.ts with its test, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (the /health bullet) and docs/CONFIGURATION.md (the environment table). Both docs files are also declared by CQ-RF07 (task-f3f364a6) and WT-17/18/19. Worktree mode merges disjoint hunks, so keep these edits to one sentence in the /health bullet and one table row.

It keeps the key bytes in memory only and deletes the variable from its own process.env. The key never reaches daemon.json, a log, the activity log, chat or any response.

`GET /health?challenge=<64 lowercase hex>` answers the normal body plus `spawnProof`, the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the key bytes over the challenge text, only while a key is held. With no key, a missing, malformed or repeated challenge, or any other query parameter, it answers the normal body without spawnProof. The Host guard still refuses first, plain `GET /health` is unchanged, and every other path still answers 426.

A new packages/moe-daemon/src/server/spawnProof.test.ts covers: key parsing (valid, short, non-hex, absent); the known-answer vector from the description; challenge parsing (valid, uppercase, short, repeated, extra parameter, no query); and the /health URL routing helper. Tests are RED first against the missing module, with the failing output quoted.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (the /health bullet) and docs/CONFIGURATION.md (the environment table: set by the IDE for a protected spawn, never by hand) describe the key and the challenge answer.

The full daemon suite `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run` exits 0 in a whole-repo git-archive snapshot of the task worktree, never in place in the shared control checkout. Its output is the complete_task evidence.
taskRails: The spawn key never leaves process memory: it is never written to daemon.json, a log, the activity log, chat or any response, and it is never echoed. Only its HMAC over a caller's challenge is returned.

implementationPlan.description:
Implement packages/moe-daemon/src/server/spawnProof.ts: pure functions, no IO, node:crypto only.
- `export const SPAWN_PROOF_ENV = 'MOE_SPAWN_PROOF_KEY'`.
- `takeSpawnProofKey(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): { key: Buffer | null; problem?: string }`. It reads env[SPAWN_PROOF_ENV], ALWAYS deletes the variable when present (valid or not), and accepts /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i as Buffer.from(value, 'hex'). Otherwise it returns a problem such as 'MOE_SPAWN_PROOF_KEY is not 64 hex characters', which must never interpolate the value.
- `parseHealthRequest(url: string | undefined): { health: false } | { health: true; challenge?: string }`. Split at the first '?'. The path part must be exactly '/health'. Parse the query with URLSearchParams and keep a challenge only when the query holds exactly one parameter, named challenge, whose value matches /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/.
- `spawnProofFor(key: Buffer, challenge: string): string` returns createHmac('sha256', key).update(challenge, 'ascii').digest('hex').
- `healthProofFields(route, key)` returns { spawnProof } or {}.
A header comment states the purpose (the VS Code protected-provenance proof, task-648a5916), the contract, and that the key is never returned or logged.

Error handling: none of these throws on hostile input. URLSearchParams decoding is safe, and anything malformed simply yields no challenge.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented stdlib-only pure helpers; GREEN snapshot run npx vitest run src/server/spawnProof.test.ts: 1 file, 36 tests passed, exit 0. Explicit length checks additionally reject final-newline values (JavaScript regex $ otherwise accepts a final newline). Key consumed/deleted for valid and invalid values; no secret interpolation, IO, or extra dependency.

implementationPlan.description:
Wire packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts.

(1) Only the `_run` path reads the key, before anything else runs: `case '_run':` (~:1240) or the top of startDaemon (~:641), which only `_run` reaches. It calls takeSpawnProofKey(process.env) once and keeps `key` in a module-level or closure variable. When there is a problem, it logs one logger.warn({ problem }) line; the value is never logged.
- The `start` and `init` supervisor (superviseDaemon) must NOT read or delete the variable. spawnChild (~:969) already passes `env: process.env` to every `_run`, crash restarts included. Leave that untouched and say so in a one-line comment.
- Deleting from process.env in `_run` keeps the key away from the processes the daemon spawns (git and the like).

(2) The HTTP handler (~:710): replace `req.method === 'GET' && req.url === '/health'` with a route from parseHealthRequest(req.url) for GET requests. Keep the isAllowedHealthHost 403 guard first, exactly as now. Build the body as today and spread healthProofFields(route, key) after bindHost. Plain `/health` stays byte-identical, and non-health paths still get 426.

(3) The key never reaches writeDaemonInfo / daemon.json, any logger call, the activity log or chat. Grep the diff for SPAWN_PROOF and key usages.

Error handling: a bad env value only logs a warning and runs without a key; the proof computation cannot throw on a validated challenge.
implementationPlan.note: Only startDaemon (_run's sole caller path) consumes/deletes the key immediately on entry, before daemon startup. Supervisor env: process.env left unchanged for initial/crash _run spawns with explanatory comment. GET uses pure route parser, existing Host 403 guard still precedes checks/stats/HMAC, optional proof spread follows unchanged bindHost. Diff/key usage audit: key stays in closure, only healthProofFields receives it; warning receives fixed problem text only; no persistence/log/chat changes. Live wiring verification follows in step-5.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A `_run` daemon started with a valid MOE_SPAWN_PROOF_KEY answers GET /health?challenge=<64 lowercase hex> with the normal body plus spawnProof, the HMAC-SHA256 of the challenge under the key bytes. It holds the key only in memory and removes it from its environment. Without a key, or for any other query, the plain body is returned; plain /health and every non-health path are unchanged.

The full daemon vitest suite exits 0 in a whole-repo snapshot.
A live smoke shows the supervisor-to-_run pass-through: the known-answer spawnProof on a challenge, none on plain /health, and the key absent from .moe.
invariants: The key is never written to daemon.json, logs, the activity log, chat or any response.
The Host guard runs before any /health work.
Plain GET /health is byte-identical, and non-health paths answer 426.
compatibility: No MCP tool contract changes. /health gains an optional field only when a challenge is sent and a key is held.
The contract and the known-answer vector are shared with task-648a5916 (the VS Code client).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Echo the key itself on /health. Rejected: it discloses the secret to anyone who can read /health. 2) Return a static hash of the key. Rejected: replayable. 3) A challenge-response HMAC over a caller-chosen 64-hex challenge, CHOSEN. It discloses nothing reusable and binds the answer to the dialled port. 4) Put the proof on the /ws handshake. Rejected: /health is already probed by both IDEs and the Host guard covers it.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The /health handler is a closure in startDaemon (index.ts ~:709) that matches req.url === '/health' exactly. isAllowedHealthHost (server/healthHost.ts) runs first. The `_run` case calls startDaemon(projectPath, port, host); `start` and `init` call superviseDaemon, whose spawnChild passes env: process.env unchanged. The client side lives in task-648a5916, which depends on this row.
planningNotes.risks: (1) `/health?anything` now answers the health body instead of 426. The DoD specifies this, and no current client sends a query. (2) /proc/<pid>/environ still shows the initial environment block of `_run`. Same-user processes are outside the threat model; do not claim more. (3) docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/CONFIGURATION.md overlap with CQ-RF07 and WT-17/18/19, so keep the hunks to one sentence and one table row. (4) The live smoke must stop only its own recorded PID.
